rebuilds.why: Round 3 (R1037). Carries r2-B's attested rebuild (round 1's option set, hint 'Use only what lines 26 to 30 tell you about him.', walk ending on the key). Held in round 2 on two executions ending on the stock sentence "In the window, line 27 answers the stem: ...", which is not exactly true: the key also needs lines 28 to 29. Both now carry the corrected executions attested in english-rewrite/stock. One line reference in a carried execution also made exact: 'any other lady' runs over lines 40 and 41.

stem.text: When Mr Darcy first walked in, the room thought very well of him. Read lines 26 to 30. Why?

options.value: Because he danced with lots of different ladies.
options.execution: Dancing every dance is Mr Bingley at line 37, carried across to Mr Darcy, who dances only twice at lines 39 and 40. Lines 27 to 29 give why the room admired Mr Darcy: his fine, tall person and handsome features, and the report of his ten thousand a year.

options.value: Because he was friendly and kind to everyone he met.
options.execution: Friendliness and kindness are nowhere in lines 26 to 30. Lines 32 and 33 find him proud and above his company, and lines 40 and 41 have him decline being introduced to any other lady.

options.value: Because he was the tallest man in the room.
options.execution: 'The tallest man in the room' is the absolute version of line 27's 'fine, tall person'.

options.value: Because he was handsome and people heard he was rich.
Because he owned a large estate in Derbyshire.
options.execution: The Derbyshire estate is at line 33, outside lines 26 to 30, and it is named only after the room has turned against him. Within the window, lines 27 to 29 give his looks and the report of his ten thousand a year.

explanationPatch.hintCore: Use only what lines 26 to 30 tell you about him.
explanationPatch._previousHintCore: What had everybody heard about him within five minutes?
explanationPatch.walkScript: Start at line 27, with 'his fine, tall person'. Line 30 says the ladies found him much handsomer than Mr Bingley. Lines 28 and 29 add the report of 'ten thousand a year'. The estate in Derbyshire comes later, at line 33. So the room liked him because he was handsome and people heard he was rich.
explanationPatch._previousWalkScript: Start at line 27, with 'his fine, tall person'. Line 29 adds 'ten thousand a year'. So his looks and his money won the room. The estate is named later.

notes.ENG-002-pp-09: r3 reviewer: the 'friendly and kind' execution cites line 32, but 'company' is on line 33. Changed 'Line 32 finds him' to 'Lines 32 and 33 find him'. Everything else is r3's rebuild, unchanged.
